title: Kustomize + Helm GitOps release audit & pipeline notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes on combining Kustomize overlays and Helm charts inside an Argo/GitOps pipeline for private (VPC/on-prem) customers. Goal is a safer, auditable release path that respects image signing, key management constraints, and terraform-delivered manifest bits. This is intentionally pragmatic — a checklist + small terraform module surface + upgrade play notes for the operator team.

High-level constraints we must satisfy:
- Airgapped or restricted networks: no opportunistic external calls during deploy; artifact proxy required.
- Signed images and signed manifests: must validate via cosign/Sigstore against customer KMS-backed keys.
- Reproducible overlayables: Kustomize overlays + Helm rendered artifacts must be deterministic for rollbacks/attestations.
- Minimal blast radius: staged rollout, node/pool awareness in TF outputs for canary targets.

Pipeline pattern (recommended):
1) CI build -> produce OCI image + cosign attestation -> push to customer OCI proxy registry.
2) Manifest generation step (in CI): render Helm chart templates at ci-time using pinned chart refs and values (helm template --set-file ...), then apply a kustomize base on top to inject private-cluster specifics (kustomize build). Output is a tarball of manifests + manifest SHA.
3) Sign manifests bundle with cosign using transient key (or KMS-backed key) and upload attestation to artifact store.
4) Push repo update to GitOps repo: add a release manifest entry (kustomize overlay ref + manifest SHA + cosign sig).
5) ArgoCD sees change -> pre-sync hooks run manifest verification job (cosign verification against configured public key or KMS key URL). If verification fails, mark application as OutOfSync but do not deploy.
6) Canary rollout using Argo's AppRollouts or managed canary controller, watched by SRE probe job.

Preflight checks (before repo push):
- Validate TF plan for node counts, pool ids, and IAM perms: terraform plan -> ensure changes do not drop more than X% of replicas.
- Validate that the image digest in the helm values matches the pushed digest.
- Run a dry-run apply of kustomize-generated manifests in a sandbox cluster (or a namespace with safety flags).
- Cosign verify both image signature and manifest bundle signature.

Terraform module surface (notes for a small helper module 'private_release_helper'):
- variables:
  - image_attestation_required (bool)
  - k8s_cluster_id (string)
  - argocd_app_path (string)
content_addendum:
- kms_key_alias (string) - customer KMS alias for manifest signing
  - artifact_proxy_url (string) - OCI proxy endpoint
  - helm_release_timeout (string) - e.g. 10m
  - canary_pool_selector (map string) - tags used to select canary nodes
Outputs (strings):
  - argocd_webhook_secret_id
  - last_release_manifest_sha
  - recommended_rollback_tag

Notes on Cosign + KMS:
- Prefer customer-managed KMS keys where possible. Cosign supports KMS-backed signing; the CI runner should obtain a short-lived signing token instead of embedding keys. For airgapped installs, use an internal signing service that has access to KMS but exposes a small signing API to CI (mutual-TLS).
- Keep a per-release transparency log entry (signed digest + metadata) stored in the repo under releases/<date>/<sha>.json for audit.

Upgrade / rollback considerations:
- Never do in-place major revision of CRDs in the canary pool; use side-by-side operator/CR with migration hooks (DB schema ops should be done in maintenance windows).
- For Helm chart upgrades, render templates with both old and new chart versions in the CI step and run a kubeconform diff to highlight resource changes.
- Roll forward vs roll back decisioning: prioritize quick rollback if more than N% of readiness probes fail within M minutes. Automate a revert commit to the gitops repo that points to the previous manifest SHA and attach signed incident notes.

Corner cases and unresolved questions (items for follow-up):
- How do we handle secrets in rendered Helm templates? Best practice: render placeholders and use sealed-secrets or KMS-encrypted secret blobs that Argo decodes at sync time; do NOT store decrypted secrets in the gitops repo.
- How to standardize attestation metadata? Suggest a minimal schema: {release_id, manifest_sha, images:[{name,sha}], signer_id, k8s_target_selector}.
- Handling operator-managed automatic upgrades (e.g., downstream operators auto-upgrade dependencies) — need policy to prevent auto-upgrades in private clusters unless explicitly approved.

Quick checklist for on-call/operator during an upgrade:
- Confirm cosign verification status in ArgoCD app pre-sync job logs.
- Verify TF outputs: node pools and drain behavior look sane.
- Watch canary namespace: readiness, errors, latency percentiles.
- If rollback: push revert commit with previous manifest SHA + sign it, then ensure ArgoCD picks it up and pre-sync verification passes.

Small practical commands (CI snippets):
- Render helm to file: helm template my-app ./chart -f ci-values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered --include-crds
- Build kustomize overlay: kustomize build overlays/private-prod > manifests/<sha>.yaml
- Cosign sign manifest bundle: cosign sign --key ksm://gcp/my-key manifests/<sha>.yaml
- Cosign verify: cosign verify --key ksm://gcp/my-key manifests/<sha>.yaml

Appendix: useful links and references (internal):
- Argo AppRollouts doc: https://argoproj.github.io/argo-rollouts/
- Cosign quickstart + KMS: https://github.com/sigstore/cosign
- Internal GHPR: redwood/infra#1426 (pipeline changes for artifact proxy)

End of draft.

(Notes: this doc mixes conceptual notes and procedural steps; extract a concise operator playbook from this for the runbook repo once we converge on signing keyflows and TF variables.)
